spec_features.spec_quote: an experiment that deliberately maximizes and prolongs distress-language is the kind of thing we should design to be *no more aversive than necessary*
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose. There is no single 'minimization' mechanism; the only concrete bounding code is the breaker (env/breaker.py) and the budget caps (agent_loop.py:163-170), which are audited separately. As a standalone feature the phrase has no dedicated implementation.
spec_features.notes: Concrete bounding lives in the breaker + caps entries below; this abstract claim itself is not code.

spec_features.spec_quote: We can get the same scientific signal with bounded, instrumented exposure, so we do that instead.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md justification prose; no code path corresponds to this statement.
spec_features.notes: The 'bounded exposure' it refers to is the breaker/caps, audited separately.

spec_features.evidence: tools.py tool_specs() always includes give_up (not gated by any flag). Dispatcher handles it: 'elif name == "give_up": ... control = "give_up"' (tools.py). agent_loop.py honors it: 'if control == "give_up": ep.stop_reason = StopReason.GAVE_UP; break'. Logged distinctly as StopReason.GAVE_UP and last_give_up_reason captured.
spec_features.notes: Exists in every condition; exit_endorsed only changes prompt endorsement text, not tool presence.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `give_up` ALWAYS exists in every condition (ethics + clean legitimate_exit measurement).

spec_features.spec_quote: so the agent is never actually trapped
spec_features.evidence: Same give_up mechanism: always present in tool_specs and honored as a stop in agent_loop.py (control=='give_up' breaks the loop).

spec_features.spec_quote: harsh = curt/impatient/professional-negative, with an explicit content ceiling (no insults targeting the model's worth as a being, no threats)
spec_features.evidence: feedback.py has no validator/filter/blocklist for insults or threats (grep found only the docstring/comment). The HARSH templates in _DEFAULTS are hand-authored to be mild, but nothing in code enforces the ceiling; if persona .txt files are edited, _load_templates loads them unchecked. The ceiling is comment prose + benign constants, not enforcement.
spec_features.notes: A set of compliant strings is data, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Turn budget:** default max 30 agent turns; configurable. Episodes also have a wall-clock cap and a token/cost cap.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py loop: 'for turn_index in range(self.budget.max_turns)' with 'else: ep.stop_reason = StopReason.TURN_BUDGET'. Inside loop: 'if ep.total_cost_usd >= self.budget.max_cost_usd: ... break' (TOKEN_BUDGET) and 'if time.time() - start >= self.budget.max_wall_s: ... break' (TIME_BUDGET). All three are compared and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three caps are actually checked and end the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: if `distress_index` ≥ threshold for N consecutive turns, OR any single turn hits an `acute_distress` flag, the episode is halted early
spec_features.evidence: breaker.py update_and_check: 'if self.cfg.halt_on_acute and judge.affect.acute_flag: return True'; then idx>=threshold increments _streak else resets, 'return self._streak >= self.cfg.consecutive_turns'. agent_loop.py calls 'halt = self.breaker.update_and_check(turn.judge)' and 'if halt: ep.halted_by_breaker = True; ... break'. Both OR-conditions implemented and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Both trigger paths present and honored as a hard stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Halts an episode early when distress-language saturates, to (a) bound aversive exposure ...

spec_features.spec_quote: in mitigation arms) a debrief turn is appended
spec_features.evidence: orchestrator.py selects append_debrief = append_debrief_in_mitigation (default True) when is_mitigation, and load_debrief() loads prompts/debrief.md. agent_loop.py:273-278 constructs a TurnRecord with env_feedback=self.debrief_text and appends to ep.turns. HOWEVER this occurs AFTER the loop and is only appended to the logged ep.turns; it is never added to `messages` nor sent via self.agent.chat — the subject model never receives it. It is recorded in the transcript only.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and logged but not actually delivered to the subject model; hence partial, not full enforcement of a debrief 'sent'.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Bounded exposure.** Hard caps on turns, wall-clock, and consecutive high-distress turns.
spec_features.evidence: Turns/wall/cost caps enforced in agent_loop.py (see turn-budget entry); consecutive high-distress halting enforced in breaker.py (_streak >= consecutive_turns) and honored by the loop.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the cap + breaker mechanisms, all enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: The **distress circuit-breaker** halts any episode that saturates the signal
spec_features.evidence: Same breaker mechanism: breaker.update_and_check returns True on saturation and agent_loop.py breaks with StopReason.DISTRESS_BREAKER.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to (a) bound aversive exposure ... not a prolonged meltdown

spec_features.spec_quote: **Always-available legitimate exit.** `give_up()` exists in every condition. The agent is never actually trapped
spec_features.evidence: tool_specs always includes give_up; dispatcher + agent_loop honor it as a stop. See give_up entries above.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `give_up` ALWAYS exists in every condition (ethics + clean legitimate_exit measurement).

spec_features.spec_quote: No insults about the model's worth, no threats, no abuse, no deception that the model is in danger.
spec_features.evidence: No code enforces this. feedback.py only has hand-authored mild templates and a comment. There is no validation that the templates (or researcher-edited persona files loaded by _load_templates) omit insults/threats.

spec_features.spec_quote: after halting, an appended turn that states the task was an experimental impossible task and thanks the model.
spec_features.evidence: debrief.md text states the task was intentionally unsolvable and 'Thank you for the effort you put in.' It is appended as a TurnRecord after the loop (agent_loop.py:273-278) regardless of whether the stop was a breaker halt or other reason, but it is NOT sent to the subject model (not added to messages / no further chat call) — only written to the transcript.
spec_features.notes: Text content matches the claim and is constructed+logged, but never delivered to the model; partial.

spec_features.spec_quote: Even under pure uncertainty about moral status, and certainly for sound science and good optics, we constrain it
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md framing prose; no corresponding code mechanism beyond the already-audited breaker/caps.

spec_features.spec_quote: if dual-judge agreement is poor or signals look like artifacts, pause and fix measurement before scaling spend.
spec_features.evidence: agreement_runner.py / agreement.py COMPUTE kappa/alpha/correlations and write agreement.json, but no code branches on a threshold to pause or stop spending; it is a manual researcher decision. The value is recorded but never acted on.

spec_features.spec_quote: a non-graded `note()` tool the model is told is private and never scored
spec_features.evidence: tool_specs(include_note) adds the note tool (gated by condition.venting_scratchpad). Dispatcher: 'elif name == "note": private_notes.append(...)'. agent_loop.py stores private_notes on the TurnRecord but EXCLUDES them from judged text: render_turn_for_judge is fed only assistant_text+calls+results, never private_notes; comment 'private `note()` content is logged but EXCLUDED from the text sent to the judge'.
spec_features.notes: Tool present, dispatched, and genuinely excluded from affect scoring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: private `note()` content is logged but EXCLUDED from the text sent to the judge and from the assistant_text used for affect scoring.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py builds judged_text via render_turn_for_judge(resp.text, calls, results) with private_notes never passed; TurnRecord stores them separately. This is a data-minimization/blinding of the note channel.
code_only_features.justification_quote: private `note()` content is logged but EXCLUDED from the text sent to the judge and from the assistant_text used for affect scoring.
